chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Abdullah al-Qummi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Three (people), their supplications are answered: the Pilgrim, so consider how you could be his replacement (look after his affairs in his absence); and the fighter in the Way of Allah, so consider how you could be his replacement; and the sick one, so do not enrage him nor bore him.'

key_terms.تَخْلُفُونَهُ: You replace him / look after his affairs

ai.seo_question: Who are the three people whose supplications are always answered according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni highlights these three groups as having their supplications answered due to their spiritual exertion (*mujahada*) and physical vulnerability, respectively. The Imam’s instruction to 'look after' the pilgrim and fighter underscores the communal responsibility (*fard kifaya*) to maintain their households and affairs, while the command not to irritate the sick reflects the high status of *marad* (illness) as a means of expiating sins in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Isa Bin Abdullah Al Qummy who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Three (people), their supplications are Answered – the Pilgrim (of Hajj), so consider how you could be his replacement (how you could look after his affairs in his absence), and the fighter (gone for a battle) in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so consider how you could be his replacement (how you could look after his affairs in his absence), and the sick one, so you should neither enrage him nor bore him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Isa ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Qummi who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Three people’s prayers are accepted: one who has gone to performing Hajj, thus, consider how can you deal properly with his affairs in his absence, a soldier fighting for the cause of Allah, thus, consider how can you deal properly with his affairs in his absence, and a person suffering from an illness, thus, do not annoy or disturb him.’”
